latin.563: Deinde non videtur Vir doctus sibi satis constare. Dixerat enim paragrapho praecedente aliquem in alio peccare ex vi vocis designare imputationem, idemque esse in alio peccare ac peccatum alienum imputari. Nunc vult esse diversa; & prius esse peccare in alio, quam peccatum alienum imputari; hocque tanquam posterius, illud supponere, tanquam prius & causam.
latin.564: Deinde passim inculcat peccatum Adami nostrum non esse nisi imputatione: unde sequitur, nos in Adamo non peccasse nisi imputatione. At tamen nunc vult peccatum Adami nobis imputari, quia nos in Adamo peccavimus. Quomodo autem in Adamo peccavimus, si peccatum Adami nostrum non fuit? Ut igitur prius in Adamo peccavimus, quam eius peccatum nobis fuit imputatum, sic prius nostrum fuit Adami peccatum, quam nobis imputaretur. Quomodo ergo passim inculcat nostrum non esse, nisi per imputationem?
latin.565: Denique Deus, inquit, imputando peccatum alicui non facit ut peccaverit. Non facit igitur Deus imputando posteros Adami esse peccatores. Nam peccator non est qui non peccavit. Quomodo ergo dicit Vir doctus peccatum actuale Adami propter imputationem, nos inobedientia Adami constitui peccatores imputatione? Uno verbo, si peccatores sumus antequam Deus nobis imputet peccatum Adami, peccatum Adami non introiit in mundum imputatione, sed imputatio introitum illum sequitur: id quod mihi erat probandum.
latin.566: Deinde tu vis omnes peccasse in Adamo. Dabis autem fuisse in Adamo quomodo in Adamo peccaverunt: prius enim est esse quam agere vel peccare. Fuimusne ergo in Adamo imputatione qua esse eius? negabis procul dubio: cur ergo vis nos in eo peccasse imputatione qua peccare ipsius?
latin.567: Dices fortasse istud peccare non significare peccatum imputari. Hinc inferam, igitur peccasse omnes peccato actuali, non quia ipsis imputetur, sed alio modo, quem mihi a te explicari cupio, qui toties negas peccatum actuale Adami nostrum esse alio modo quam per imputationem.
latin.568: Sed praeterea quaero. Quando peccavimus in Adamo eius peccato actuali? an cum illud peccavit, an alio tempore? haud dubie cum illud commisit in paradiso: nullum aliud tempus assignare potes. Audi quid inde sequatur. Qui peccarunt ita ut iustam condemnationem mortis aeternae sibi commeriti sint, illi vere & proprie peccarunt. Qui autem vere & proprie peccarunt, illi tunc cum peccaverunt vere & proprie fuerunt. Qui ergo hodie incipit esse & nascitur infans, ille vere & proprie loquendo fuit iam tum, cum Adamus esset in paradiso, ante aliquot annorum millia: quippe qui tum vere & proprie peccavit. Itaque quod de se dixit Christus Ioh. 8. 58. Antequam Abraham nasceretur ego sum, nemo fuerit nostrum, qui idem dicere de semetipso non possit.

pass_a.563: Placeus: the opponent will not hold together. He first made 'sin in another' mean the same as alien-sin imputation; now he splits them and puts in-another sinning before imputation as its cause. The shift from identity to priority undercuts his own prior paragraph.
pass_a.564: He repeats that Adam's act is ours only by imputation—so we sinned in Adam only by imputation—yet also that it is imputed because we sinned in him. If it was not yet ours, how did we sin in him? The order he needs makes it ours before imputation, against his own refrain.
pass_a.565: He grants God does not make someone to have sinned by imputing. Then imputation does not make Adam's posterity sinners. If we are already sinners before God imputes Adam's act, that act did not enter by imputation—imputation follows the entry. That is Placeus's point.
pass_a.566: You say all sinned in Adam. Being is prior to acting. You will not say we were in Adam by an imputation of his being; why then sin in him by an imputation of his sinning?
pass_a.567: If you retreat and say 'to sin' here does not mean 'to have sin imputed,' then all sinned by the actual act in some other mode—which you must name, having always denied any mode but imputation.
pass_a.568: I press the time: we sinned that actual act only when he committed it in paradise—you have no other hour. Whoever so sinned as to merit just eternal death then truly and properly sinned, and so then truly and properly was. On that reading today's newborn already was in paradise millennia ago, and each of us could speak Christ's Before Abraham was born, I am. Tip before GAR treats the reductio as jest.

563: Next the learned man does not seem to himself to stand consistent enough. For he had said in the preceding paragraph that for someone to sin in another designates imputation by force of the word, and that to sin in another and for another's sin to be imputed are the same. Now he will have them to be diverse; and that to sin in another is prior to another's sin being imputed; and that this as the later, that as the prior and cause.
564: Next he inculcates everywhere that Adam's sin is not ours except by imputation: whence it follows that we did not sin in Adam except by imputation. And yet now he will have Adam's sin imputed to us, because we sinned in Adam. But how did we sin in Adam, if Adam's sin was not ours? Therefore as we first sinned in Adam before his sin was imputed to us, so Adam's sin was first ours before it was imputed to us. How then does he inculcate everywhere that it is not ours except by imputation?
565: Finally God, he says, by imputing sin to someone does not make him to have sinned. Therefore God by imputing does not make Adam's posterity to be sinners. For he is not a sinner who has not sinned. How then does the learned man say that by Adam's actual sin, because of imputation, we are constituted sinners by Adam's disobedience by imputation? In one word, if we are sinners before God imputes Adam's sin to us, Adam's sin did not enter into the world by imputation, but imputation follows that entry: which was what I had to prove.
566: Next you will have all to have sinned in Adam. But you will grant that they were in Adam in the way they sinned in Adam: for it is prior to be than to act or to sin. Were we therefore in Adam by an imputation of his being? You will deny it far from doubt: why then will you have us to have sinned in him by an imputation of his sinning?
567: You will perhaps say that that to sin does not signify sin to be imputed. From this I will infer, therefore all sinned by actual sin, not because it is imputed to them, but in another way, which I desire to be explained to me by you, who so often deny that Adam's actual sin is ours in any other way than by imputation.
568: But besides I ask. When did we sin in Adam by his actual sin? when he sinned it, or at another time? without doubt when he committed it in paradise: you can assign no other time. Hear what follows from that. Those who have so sinned that they have merited for themselves the just condemnation of eternal death, those have truly and properly sinned. But those who have truly and properly sinned, those then when they sinned were truly and properly. Therefore he who today begins to be and is born an infant, he truly and properly speaking already then was, when Adam was in paradise, some thousands of years before: inasmuch as he then truly and properly sinned. And so what Christ said of himself, John 8. 58. Before Abraham was born I am, there will be none of us who cannot say the same of himself.
